chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdillāh, who said:

ʿAbdullāh ibn Hulayl used to hold the view regarding ʿAbdullāh. Then he went to al-ʿAskar and retracted from that. So I asked him about the reason for his retraction, and he said: “I presented to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام that I should ask him about that. Then he met me in a narrow road and inclined toward me. When he came alongside me, he directed toward me something from his mouth, and it fell upon my chest. I took it, and it was a parchment upon which was written: ‘It was not there, nor was it so.’”

key_terms.أَبِي الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Abū al-Ḥasan, the Imam addressed with the honorific peace be upon him (AS)
key_terms.الْعَسْكَرِ: the military quarter, referring to the place associated with the Imam
key_terms.رَقٌّ: a parchment or thin written sheet
key_terms.رُجُوعِهِ: his retraction or return from a previously held belief
key_terms.طَرِيقٍ ضَيِّقٍ: a narrow road or passage where the encounter took place
key_terms.مَا كَانَ هُنَالِكَ: it was not there, a negation of the claimed status
key_terms.وَلَا كَذَلِكَ: nor was it so, further denying the claim

ai.seo_question: How did ʿAbdullāh ibn Hulayl retract his view about the claim to the Imamate?
ai.summary: This report describes how ʿAbdullāh ibn Hulayl abandoned a prior belief concerning the Imamate after receiving a written indication from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام. The narration serves as an account used to distinguish the true Imam from a false claimant in the matter of religious authority.
